source.author: hor
source.text: Deus inde ego, furum aviumque maxima formido; nam fures dextra coercet obscaenoque ruber porrectus ab inguine palus, ast inportunas volucres in vertice harundo terret fixa vetatque novis considere in hortis.
source.text_original: Deus inde ego, furum aviumque  / maxima formido; nam fures dextra coercet  / obscaenoque ruber porrectus ab inguine palus,  / ast inportunas volucres in vertice harundo  / terret fixa vetatque novis considere in hortis.
source.text_english: Then I am a god, the greatest terror of thieves and birds; for on the right side a red stake restrains thieves, thrust out from the foul groin, while a reed fixed on my head frightens away troublesome birds and prevents them from settling in the new gardens.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Maluit esse deum: deus inde ego, furum aviumque, Maxima formido...
reuse.text_original: Maluit esse deum: deus inde ego, furum aviumque, Maxima formido...
reuse.text_english: He preferred to be a god: from that point I am a god, the greatest terror of thieves and birds...
